## Step 1: a declared server read in an action's param dialog (no code written)

Tree: `objectstack-ai/objectstack` `origin/main` `4ed20928` (the Claim's pin). Every line number below is at `4ed20928`. Nothing was edited, committed or pushed.

**Headline.** The premise holds: no action key declares a pre-submit read, and the one companion is hardcoded (`actionDialogCompanion.ts:37-46`, `sys_user` + `ban_user` only). The spec already has the read grammar this needs: the page element's `ElementApiDataSourceSchema` (`packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts:520`) refuses a non-same-origin URL, a non-`GET` method and credential keys at parse, and its console half (`ui/packages/react/src/element-data-source/useElementApiDataSource.ts`) re-judges stored metadata with that schema before it reads. I recommend **one new action key, `preflight`, built on that grammar** (option A below). The `ban_user` panel **cannot** be carried by a read-only declaration without forcing it, because half of it is a repeatable bulk write; I propose it stays host chrome in the same companion slot (item 3). That changes the card's Work item 2 and one clause of Done-when, so it needs the seat's acceptance.

### 1. Census: where a param dialog is composed, and what each draws today

| # | Composer | Site | Draws above the params | Reaches a companion? |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `useConsoleActionRuntime` (object views, list rows, ConsoleShell's `onParamCollection`) | `ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:269` (handler), `:375` (companion), `:1014` (render) | title, description (with the admin-override notice first), the companion | yes, via `resolveParamDialogCompanion` |
| 2 | `RecordDetailView` (record page header and related-list rows) | `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx:1536` (handler), `:1608` (companion), `:5451` (render) | title, description, the companion | yes, same resolver |
| 3 | `MetadataTypeActions` (type-level actions from `/meta/types`: ResourceEditPage header, ResourceListPage toolbar) | `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/MetadataTypeActions.tsx:136-139` (`collectParams`), `:328` (render) | title only: no description, no `run`, no companion | no |
| 4 | `BulkActionDialog` (grid bulk actions, its own dialog, not `ActionParamDialog`) | `ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/components/BulkActionDialog.tsx:446` (params step) | params step, then a confirm step listing the affected rows | no |

The shared renderer is `ActionParamDialog` (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ActionParamDialog.tsx`): the companion slot sits at the top of the one scrolling region (`:721-725`), values are seeded once per open from `defaultValue` (`:583-597`), and a `carryOver` param is drawn as a read-only summary and submitted verbatim (`CarryOverParam`, `:417`). Composers 1 and 2 are the only ones a record action's dialog reaches, and both already pick the companion through one function, so the two runtimes cannot disagree.

### 2. The declaration proposed for the spec child

#### Option A (recommended): `ActionSchema.preflight`, one read that both shows and seeds

```ts
preflight: {
  read: { url: string, method?: 'GET' },   // same-origin path template
  path?: string,                            // dotted path into the answer
  fields?: Array of { path, label?, format? },   // ResultDialog's field row, reused
  seed?: Array of { param, path },          // answer value -> param value
}
```

- **URL template.** `read.url` reuses `SAME_ORIGIN_API_PATH_RE` and its class-naming refusal from `page.zod.ts:391-445` (moved to one shared module both schemas import, so there is one same-origin rule, not two). It opens with a single `/`, so a template opening with a hole (`${ctx.origin}/…`) is refused by the same regex. Holes are the runner's existing grammar (`ActionRunner.ts:3059`, `interpolateTarget`, every value `encodeURIComponent`'d), closed to `${param.NAME}`, `${ctx.recordId}` and `${ctx.record.FIELD}`. `${result.*}` is refused (there is no answer before the read).
- **GET only.** `method` is `z.literal('GET')`, as on the element read. `headers`, `auth`, `token`, `credentials`, `apiKey` are refused with the element's no-credentials guidance; `body` and `params` get the element's guidance too. The console reads with its own signed-in fetch.
- **Render target.** The panel sits in the existing companion slot, above the params. `path` selects the sub-tree (the element's `ELEMENT_API_RESPONSE_PATH_RE`, `page.zod.ts:448`). `fields` reuses `resultDialog.fields`' row shape and its `format` set (`action.zod.ts:1689-1717`), so no new display vocabulary. Omitted, the selected answer is shown as JSON, as `resultDialog` does.
- **Answer to param.** Each `seed` writes the value at `path` (relative to the selected sub-tree) into the named param. A seeded param is drawn as the `carryOver` read-only summary and submitted verbatim: the user does not type it and cannot edit it. Marking it `required` is what blocks Confirm while the read is loading or has failed. No new gating key is needed.
- **Runtime contract the ui half owes.** The console reads once all holes have values, and reads again when a param named in a hole changes. On every URL change it clears the seeded values. A seed is applied only from the answer to the current URL, so what is submitted is what was shown. Stored metadata is re-judged with the spec schema before any request (as `judgeElementApiDataSource` does), and the interpolated URL is re-checked with `isSameOriginApiTarget` (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/apiActionDoor.ts:69`).

**How it is refused.** All checks run at `ActionSchema` parse, so they fire wherever an action is parsed: `defineStack`, `os validate`, and a metadata save, which answers the ADR-0112 `VALIDATION_ERROR` envelope with the issue path (`preflight.read.url`, `preflight.seed.0.param`, …):

1. `read.url` is not a same-origin path: regex, which projects into the published JSON Schema as `pattern`. The message names the class (scheme, `//`, backslash, space or control, relative).
2. `read.method` is not `GET`: literal.
3. A credential-shaped or unknown key: `strictObject` guidance.
4. A hole outside the closed set, or a `${param.NAME}` naming no declared param: `superRefine`. This is cross-key, so it cannot be a `pattern`.
5. `preflight` on an action with no non-empty `params`: no dialog would open. This is the same rule `submitText` already follows (`action.zod.ts:1520`).
6. A `seed.param` naming no declared param, a param seeded twice, a seeded param that also declares `defaultValue`, `defaultFromRow` or `carryOver`, or a seeded param read by a hole (a cycle).

At runtime, a refused or failed read draws an error panel naming which. Seeded params stay empty, and their `required` mark blocks Confirm. The preflight is UX, not authorization: the action's own endpoint must still check the seeded token.

**What an author writes (cloud consumer).** NOT MEASURED: cloud is unreadable from this account, so the action and param names and the answer shape are taken from the card text (`findings`, `verdict.findingSet`).

```ts
{
  name: 'install_package',
  type: 'api',
  target: '/api/v1/cloud/packages/${ctx.recordId}/install',
  params: [
    { name: 'environment_id', type: 'lookup', reference: 'sys_environment', required: true },
    { name: 'version', type: 'text', required: true },
    { name: 'confirm_schema_upgrade', label: 'Schema change confirmation', type: 'text', required: true },
  ],
  preflight: {
    read: { url: '/api/v1/cloud/packages/${ctx.recordId}/upgrade-plan?environment_id=${param.environment_id}&version=${param.version}' },
    path: 'data',
    fields: [{ path: 'findings', label: 'Schema findings', format: 'json' }],
    seed: [{ param: 'confirm_schema_upgrade', path: 'verdict.findingSet' }],
  },
}
```

#### Option B: two keys on existing surfaces

This option adds an action-level `preview` holding a page component whose `dataSource` is an element API binding, rendered by `SchemaRenderer` with the stat, checklist and usage-bar blocks. It also adds a param-level `seedFrom: { read, path }`. It needs `ElementApiDataSourceSchema.read.url` widened to take holes, which also changes a published page-element surface that has no param scope. The shown answer and the seeded value would come from two declarations that must name the same URL.

#### Four axes (pm-dispatch SKILL.md block, as the brief carries it)

- **Real business need.** The one measured consumer is cloud#3863 / cloud#4038: one read, a findings list and one token to carry. A covers exactly that. B's rich block rendering has no measured pull, and `ban_user` is not a consumer either (item 3).
- **Long-term soundness.** A is one declaration and one request whose answer is both shown and submitted. It shares the element read's same-origin rule and refusal text through one module, so there is no second rule. B widens a published page grammar for a need pages do not have.
- **Keeping AI from writing it wrong.** In A every cross-reference (hole to param, seed to param) is checked at parse inside one key. In B, two keys must agree on one URL, and nothing can check that the shown read and the seeding read are the same request: that is the drift an AI author makes.
- **Startup-stage scope.** A adds one key with four members and reuses `resultDialog`'s field row. It has no `title`: the panel takes a generic translated heading, and a title is a later widening with pull. B adds two keys plus a grammar widening.

**Recommendation: A.** The axes do not conflict.

### 3. Re-expressing `ban_user` (Work item 2): it cannot be carried without forcing

`UserAssignedWorkPanel` (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/UserAssignedWorkPanel.tsx`) does two things:

- **A read.** `security.assignedWork.count` (`GET /api/v1/security/users/:id/assigned-work`, `:99`).
- **A write.** `security.assignedWork.transfer` (`POST …/assigned-work/transfer`, `:152`). The write has its own user picker, moves at most 500 records per click, can be repeated, and re-reads the counts after each batch. It runs independently of the ban's Confirm and never gates it.

A GET-only declaration cannot carry the write, by design (Work item 3).

The read half is not a clean fit either. The panel labels each object through metadata (`servedObjectLabel`), names the objects the administrator cannot read, flags a truncated count, and splits owned from assigned work (`userAssignedWork.ts`). Generic `fields` rows cannot draw any of that without new formats. Splitting the panel into a declared count plus a host-chrome transfer would make host chrome refresh a declared read, which ties the two mechanisms together.

**Proposal.** `ban_user` stays host chrome, as one panel. "One mechanism" is kept at the **slot**: `ParamDialogCompanion` becomes a union of the host-chrome `user-assigned-work` and the declared `preflight`. Both are drawn by the same slot and picked by the same `resolveParamDialogCompanion`, which reads `action.preflight` for the declared kind. If an action ever carries both, both are drawn, the declared read first; none does today. This amends Work item 2, and the Done-when clause "`ban_user` keeps its behaviour through the same declaration" becomes "`ban_user` keeps its behaviour, as host chrome in the same companion slot". That amendment is the seat's or the maintainer's to accept.

### 4. Declarations

- **Spec child:** `Metadata-protocol: added` (new authorable key `ActionSchema.preflight`), `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, a `minor` changeset on `@objectstack/spec`. `Skills-docs:` is owed. `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md` documents the action keys and is the place for `preflight`; the spec child's author confirms that with a `git grep`.
- **The ui half (this card, after the child lands):** `Metadata-protocol: none` (it implements the spec's key and adds none). `Clause-②: yes (widening)` if it adds `@object-ui/i18n` keys, as the panel heading, loading and failure text will (common rule 11, all ten packs). The changeset is `patch`.

### 5. Split and dependency

**Spec child (spec lane):**

- `packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts`: the `preflight` key and refusals 1 to 6.
- One shared module for `SAME_ORIGIN_API_PATH_RE`, its refusal, the response-path regex and the no-credentials text. `page.zod.ts` imports it, so the page element's accept set and messages stay byte-identical.
- Tests: the cloud example parses green, plus one refusal per class with its issue path.
- The liveness row `preflight: planned` in `packages/spec/liveness/action.json` (naming this card as the consumer).
- The Studio action form row or omit row (`action.form.ts`, `metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts`).
- Generated artifacts: `gen:schema`, `gen:docs`, and `gen:api-surface` if the shared module exports.
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx` and the skills line.

**This ui card, after the child lands:**

- `actionDialogCompanion.ts`: the union.
- `ActionParamDialog.tsx`: the panel, seed apply, stale-answer guard, and the seeded param drawn read-only.
- Both handlers (`useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx`, `RecordDetailView.tsx`): forward `action.preflight` and a URL interpolator. `substituteScopeTokens` is module-private in `ui/packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts:3363`, so the ui card either exports it or passes the runner's `ctx` through `ParamCollectionHandler`. That is a `ui/packages/core` file the build surface must name.
- Reuse of `readElementApi` and `selectElementApiPath` from `@object-ui/react`.
- Tests pinning the cloud-shaped flow and `ban_user` unchanged.
- i18n keys in all ten packs.
- The liveness flip `planned` to `live`. This is a `packages/spec/liveness/**` edit, so the seat must allow it on the ui card's surface, or the spec child owns the flip.
- `node scripts/check-sdui-manifest.mjs`.

**Dependency.** This card is `Blocked-by: SPEC_CHILD`. The Console type-checks against the workspace spec, so the ui PR cannot open green before the child merges.

**Open questions for the seat:**

1. Do you accept the item 3 amendment to Work item 2 and Done-when?
2. Do composers 3 (`MetadataTypeActions`) and 4 (`BulkActionDialog`) draw the preflight? I recommend no for both on this card. Composer 3's type-level actions have no pull. On composer 4 there is no single row to read, so the spec child should also refuse `preflight` beside `execution: 'aggregate'`. That would be refusal 7, and it is the spec owners' call.
3. Who owns the liveness flip: the ui card, with a surface exception, or the spec child?

## Claim amendment · step 1 accepted · card parked on its spec child · 2026-11-09T06:27Z

This amends claim 6733653625 on #31808, after the dev's step-1 report 6733724428. The premise holds, and the cited files are unchanged from `4ed20928` to `ad622d30f`.

- **Shape: option A is accepted.** `ActionSchema.preflight` is one same-origin GET whose answer is both shown above the params and seeded into a param. Its same-origin rule is shared with the page element read through one module. The spec child is **#31840** (`domain:spec`, p3, `pm:queue`), and it carries the shape, refusals 1–6 and the declarations.
- **The `ban_user` amendment is accepted.** The panel's transfer is a repeatable write, and its read needs metadata labels that generic `fields` rows cannot draw, so it stays host chrome. "One mechanism" holds at the slot: `ParamDialogCompanion` becomes a union of `user-assigned-work` and `preflight`, both drawn by the same slot and picked by `resolveParamDialogCompanion`.
  - Work item 2 now reads: "`ban_user` keeps its panel as host chrome in the same companion slot".
  - Done-when now reads: "`ban_user` keeps its behaviour, as host chrome in the same companion slot".
- **Q2: composers 3 and 4 stay out of this card.** Refusal 7 (`preflight` beside `execution: 'aggregate'`) is on #31840 as the spec owners' call. The seat recommends refusing it, because no surface draws it there.
- **Q3: the ui card flips liveness.** #31840 adds the row as `planned`, naming this card. This card flips it to `live` in its own PR, and `packages/spec/liveness/action.json` is allowed on its surface for that one row.
- **Build surface, once #31840 merges:**
  - `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/{actionDialogCompanion.ts,ActionParamDialog.tsx}`;
  - `ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx` and `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx` (both handlers);
  - `ui/packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` (export `substituteScopeTokens`, or pass the runner `ctx` through `ParamCollectionHandler`; the builder picks one and says which);
  - `ui/packages/i18n` (all ten packs, plus `zh-Hant` by `gen:zh-hant`);
  - the liveness row;
  - tests that pin the cloud-shaped flow and `ban_user` unchanged.
  - Declarations: `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (the new `@object-ui/i18n` keys), a `patch` changeset, and `Fixes #31808`.
- **State:** `Blocked-by: #31840`. The card moves `pm:dispatched` → `pm:blocked` and the assignee is cleared. No branch was pushed (`claude/project-thread-pbmpmc` has no commits). The step-1 report is the hand-over: the unlock sweep returns this card to the queue when #31840 merges, and whichever ui seat picks it up builds from this amendment.
